subject: Hosted quickstart: endpoint partitioning & rate-slice confirmation
messages:
From: Alan Zhou <alan@bytecart.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Lang <rebecca@bytecart.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Sep 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo questions — Hosted evaluation

Hey Irene,

Thanks again for the demo today — really helpful walkthrough. After chatting with the team we think Hosted is the preferred path to move quickly, but we need to lock down a few operational details before we commit to a sandbox pilot:

- Endpoints: do you give a single sandbox endpoint or multiple logical endpoints (chat vs. classification vs. embeddings)? We want to isolate features so we can route traffic separately.
- Rate limits: what are the default per-endpoint QPS/token-rate ceilings for trials, and can we request a higher "slice" for short spikes during load tests?
- Burst behavior: is there a documented burst window and throttling response shape (429 vs queuing)?
- Caching: any support for prefix/KV caching on Hosted to reduce token costs during evaluation?
- Auth/IP allowlist: we have a security gate that wants IP allowlisting and a simple integration flow (API keys + rotation). Is that supported for a sandbox?

We can share a traffic profile (QPS and payload sizes) — attaching a rough spreadsheet. Would appreciate a brief ops runbook so our infra folks know what to expect. Can we schedule a short technical sync this week with Jordan and someone from your ops team?

Thanks,
Alan
Director of Engineering
ByteCart

Attachment: bytecart-traffic-profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Zhou <alan@bytecart.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Sep 2029 15:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions — Hosted evaluation

Hi Alan — great to hear Hosted is the likely path. Quick recap and proposed next steps below; I copied Jordan (solutions) and Marissa (customer success) so we can align on ops and onboarding.

Short answers up front:
- Endpoints: we provision logical endpoints by route — common pattern is one endpoint per surface (chat, embeddings, classification). We create sandbox/staging/production routes for each logical surface.
- Rate slices: trials start with a default slice (10 QPS per endpoint, 20k tokens/min aggregate) but we can temporarily increase a slice for a scheduled load test — usually a 1–2 hour elevated window.
- Burst: we allow short bursts above the slice for up to 30s with graceful queuing; sustained excess triggers 429s. We’ll include the exact throttle curve in the runbook.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching is available on Hosted; we can suggest cache keys during the quickstart to reduce replicated generation.
- IP allowlist & auth: sandbox keys support IP allowlisting and API key rotation. For VPC-only needs we’d look at Private, but many customers meet security gates with IP allowlist + SOC2 evidence.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical sync — 30 minutes: Jordan + Marissa + your infra lead — pick a slot this week.
2) Share traffic profile (thanks for the spreadsheet) — Jordan will map endpoints to traffic buckets.
3) I’ll attach a short Hosted quickstart runbook (ops checklist + expected throttle behaviors).
4) If you need a higher trial slice, confirm target QPS and window; we’ll open a temporary elevated slice and track it.

I attached the Hosted quickstart runbook for your infra team — it contains the endpoint naming convention, ratecap matrix, and how cache/prefixing is configured.

Two scheduling options for the sync:
- Tue 9/10 10:00–10:30 PT
- Wed 9/11 14:00–14:30 PT

Which works for you?

Best,
Irene
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart-runbook.pdf (ops runbook)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Zhou <alan@bytecart.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Sep 2029 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions — Hosted evaluation

Hi Alan — Jordan here (solutions). A couple of clarifications from the ops side so you can fine-tune the traffic spreadsheet:

- Endpoint mapping: we recommend three logical endpoints to start: /chat (conversational, uses streaming), /embed (batch embeddings), /classify (short prompt classification). Each gets its own sandbox/staging/production route and independent rate slice.
- Default trial rate slice: 10 QPS per endpoint or 2 concurrent streaming connections, whichever is limiting. Token ceilings are enforced at a tenant level (example: 20k tokens/min) — we can open a separate token pool for heavy embedding runs on request.
- Elevated windows: request at least 48 hours notice for >2x baseline; we typically grant 1–4 hour elevated windows up to 3x baseline for load tests. We monitor in real-time and will escalate if the cluster is saturated.
- Throttle shape: short spikes are queued (measured latency increases), but sustained overloads result in 429s. We’ll include the exact curve and 95/99 latency SLAs per endpoint in the doc.
- Network/security: sandbox supports IP allowlist and key rotation. For stricter controls (dedicated IP ranges, on-prem), we’d talk about Dedicated or Private.

If you send the final QPS per endpoint and a couple sample payload sizes, I’ll produce a recommended endpoint-to-slice mapping and a proposed elevated-window schedule. I dropped a quick mapping template in the drive link Irene shared.

-Jordan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alan Zhou <alan@bytecart.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Rebecca Lang <rebecca@bytecart.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Sep 2029 17:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions — Hosted evaluation

Thanks Irene/Jordan — useful detail. Wed 9/11 14:00 PT works for us (Rebecca and I).

Quick data points we’ll bring to the sync:
- Baseline traffic: /chat ~ 6 QPS, median payload ~ 350 tokens, peak concurrent long-poll ~ 8 connections.
- Embeddings: /embed batch jobs ~ 30k vectors over 2 hours during nightly processing (payloads small, but CPU-heavy).
- Classification: /classify ~ 15 QPS short prompts.
- Security ask: SOC2 + IP allowlist will meet 80% of our requirements; for anything beyond (dedicated IP ranges or VPC peer) we’ll re-evaluate for a later phase.

We’ll upload a cleaned traffic profile before the sync. Please include the proposed elevated-window for a 2-hour embedding run — we want to validate cost and performance under that pattern.

See you Wed.
Alan
